brief: A hyperreal chiffon dupatta caught mid-twirl against an impossibly green alpine slope. Its fabric is translucent shocking magenta overlapping into saffron and peacock blue. Successive watercolour glazes build the fabric, so each fold where two layers cross deepens into a richer secondary hue. Gold zari borders are stitched in tiny metallic pen dots. The meadow behind is parrot green and lime, softly blurred with a few crisp buttercups in the foreground. The light is high and bright with a gentle haze. The composition is diagonal and windswept, and the feeling is euphoric, cinematic and melodramatic.

The view from directly beneath an open black umbrella, its gilt-tipped ribs radiating like an Art Deco sunburst. Bright midday light glows through the taut nylon, turning it from jet black at the hub to a smoky bronze translucence at the edges. Dense gouache-like watercolour lays the panels, and fine metallic-gold hatching follows each rib's curve. Every stitch and tension wrinkle is crisp. Strict radial symmetry is broken only by a single droplet trail. Elegant, glamorous, geometric.

A single hand-thrown stoneware tea bowl sitting slightly off-centre on a rough cedar plank. Its iron-brown body runs with a natural ash glaze that pools into glassy olive drips near the foot. Soft charcoal mass models the heavy clay, and watercolour washes of raw umber, persimmon and celadon are layered and allowed to bloom slightly. Throwing rings, thumb dents, a kiln-grit pock and a hairline crackle are all rendered with reverent precision. The light is low and wintry from a paper window. The mood is humble, tactile and unhurried. Plank grain fades into loose, warm grey at the edges.

A hyperreal hand-painted Talavera sink basin is set in a tiled countertop, viewed from above at an angle. Its cobalt and ochre glaze has been brushed thickly and has pooled into glassy ridges. A dripping brass tap hangs over three cut Persian limes and a bead-filled soap dish. Watercolour carries the glaze, with saturated cobalt pooling darker at the stroke ends and tiny pinholes in the milky white tin glaze. Water droplets are rendered with crisp highlight and refraction. The light is bright Mexican midday through a shuttered window. The mood is fresh, domestic and tactile.

A single battered leather work boot with a frayed lace, seen from slightly above. It is rendered as a hyperreal white-line wood engraving. The ground is a dense velvety black, and all form emerges through fine white pen lines that follow every contour of creased leather, cracked toe cap and stitched welt. Lines tighten for highlights and thin out into darkness for shadow, with crisp tooled crosshatch on the sole tread. There is no colour, no blur and no wash. The mood is sober, earnest and artisanal.

A hyperreal overhead view of an empty ice rink just after skating. The deep blue-black ice is laid down as dense charcoal mass, and frosty white pencil cuts across it in fine scratches. Some tracks run straight and fast, others curl into tight spirals where a skater spun. Short stubby gouges mark stops, and branching forks mark crossovers. Tiny shaved snow ridges catch the highlight along each blade line. A few dropped glove fibres and a coin-sized chip are rendered precisely. The light is cold fluorescent from above. The mood is hushed, scientific and quietly kinetic.

A tall, narrow stack of folded terry towels, rendered hyperreally but organised like a paint-swatch card. Each towel is one step darker in a single family, running from pale celadon down to deep bottle green. The towels are separated by razor-straight, tape-masked edges of bare cream paper. Fills are opaque, layered watercolour pushed to gouache density, with looped pile texture picked out in tiny pencil curls. Small marker-printed colour names and code numbers sit in a white margin to the right. The light is flat, shadowless showroom light. The mood is clinical, orderly and quietly obsessive.

A hyperreal close crop of the rolled arm of a moss-green velvet armchair. A palm print has been pressed into the pile, revealing lighter silvery nap where the fibres are bent the other way. The pile is rendered with dense short directional hatching laid in a flowing field, and soft charcoal mass deepens the troughs into near-black forest green. The highlights shimmer chartreuse. A single brass upholstery tack and a stray cat hair are rendered precisely. The light is warm lamplight from the side. The mood is plush, quiet and sensual.

Grains of sea salt, sugar crystals and tiny glass seed beads, each rendered with lens-sharp hyperreal precision. They are arranged by tweezer into a meticulous radial rosette, like a Victorian diatomist's slide, and float on a deep blue-black darkfield ground. Every cube edge, internal fracture and refraction is drawn in fine technical pen stipple and hairline white-pencil highlights. Faint rainbow fringes of cerulean and rose madder sit at the crystal rims. The mood is scientific, silent and patient. The background is dense and absolute, and a pale circular slide boundary is just visible at the edge.

A hyperreal close view of the curving hood of a lowrider coated in candy-apple red over silver metalflake. Dense spray speckles render the glitter under deep lacquer, and inside the paint sits a warped mirror reflection of palm fronds and a dusk-orange sky. Across the surface run hand-pulled pinstripes in cream and gold leaf. They are fine, tapering teardrops, mirrored curls and long sweeping lines, each rendered as a crisp, single-pass pen line. A chrome hood ornament edge glints at the top. The mood is cruising, proud and slow.

A hyperreal three-quarter view of a bandoneón resting half-open. Its black lacquered ends show worn mother-of-pearl buttons, and its bellows are folded with gilt-edged corner leather. Every scuff, fingerprint smear and crease is rendered in fine pen and smooth graded marker. Framing the instrument in the four corners, fileteado scrollwork curls inward in crisp liner strokes. It has acanthus whips, tight ribbons and shaded volutes in carmine, emerald and gold ochre, each with a fine white highlight line. The background is soft sprayed black-to-oxblood. The mood is nostalgic, theatrical and tango-tinged.

A hyperreal row of hairy coconuts perched on red-and-white striped wooden cups at a fairground shy. They are painted with the swagger of a hand-lettered sign. The stripes are bold, flat marker in vermilion and chrome yellow. The coconut husks get obsessive, fibrous pen work, and each shell carries one confident white enamel highlight laid on like a sign-writer's flick. Every object sports a hard, offset drop-shadow in deep ultramarine. Behind them, a scuffed board backdrop shows brush-drag texture and chipped gloss. The palette is loud, primary and sugary. Edges are crisp and showmanly, and the realism feels exaggerated for distance.

A single opened tin of sardines, rendered with startling hyperreal accuracy: oily silver-blue fish skins, the curled lid, and the printed label slightly scuffed. It sits isolated on a flat field of burnished gold leaf like a sacred icon. The gold ground shows square leaf seams, tiny cracks and rubbed patches revealing red bole underneath. Lay it in Naples yellow, yellow ochre and raw sienna watercolour, punctuated with sharp white pencil burnish lines. The fish are built in cool glazes of cobalt, silver grey and olive oil yellow. The contrast between the humble object and the reverent ground is the mood.

Ordinary breakfast things float weightless on a stark bone-white void, tilted on a dynamic diagonal: a slab of buttered toast, a black coffee cup seen square from above, a red paperback, a thin yellow strip of lemon peel. Each is an almost flat geometric plane laid in crisp marker colour, then given startling photographic realism through pencil shading, crumbs and surface gloss. There is no table and no ground, only soft contact shadows hovering beneath. Asymmetric, airy and revolutionary-calm.

An empty old barbershop at closing time, rendered hyperreally. A cracked oxblood leather chair sits under a single bare-bulb wall sconce, with mirrors multiplying the room behind it. The tungsten light is heavy amber and falls off fast into deep umber corners. Use charcoal mass for the shadows and layered burnt sienna, cadmium orange and raw umber watercolour for the lit zones. Chrome footrests, combs in blue Barbicide and hair clippings on chequered linoleum are sharpened with pencil. The light is warm without glowing. The mood is quiet, cinematic and lived-in, framed off-axis from a doorway.

A tumbler of water on a scarred oak kitchen table at morning, low sun striking it from the side. A spectral fan spills across the wood grain in clean bands of cadmium red, orange, lemon, viridian, ultramarine and violet. Wet-on-dry watercolour glazes keep the colours luminous and overlapping where they cross knots in the grain. Fine graphite defines the glass rim, refracted table edge and tiny bubbles clinging inside. Long diagonal composition, the glass pushed to the upper left, the spectrum taking the lower right. Clear, scientific, breakfast-quiet.

A heap of roasted cashews on a saffron-dyed cotton cloth, painted with obsessive photographic accuracy. Each nut's curled teardrop shape is a boteh, and the nuts nest into one another in swirling paisley rhythms that spiral out from an off-centre hollow. Layered transparent watercolour glazes in raw umber, burnt sienna and buttery Naples yellow build the toasted skins, with tiny reserved highlights for the oil sheen. A fine sepia pen picks out salt crystals and hairline fissures. The cloth's woven paisley print fades into soft wet-in-wet bleeds at the edges. Warm, intimate, spice-scented.

A pomegranate split open on slate, its cavity rendered as if it were crystal. Each aril is a faceted garnet gem, painted with watercolour glazes of alizarin crimson, rose madder and deep claret. Sharp white highlights are left as bare paper, and fine pen lines draw the internal facets. The pith walls are pale, banded and chalcedony-like, and the leathery rind is mottled in oxblood and ochre. The fruit fills the frame with its jagged break off-centre. Jewel-cold yet juicy.

A hyperreal overhead view of a kukui-nut lei coiled into a loose spiral on a woven lauhala mat. The nuts are polished to a deep black-brown lacquer, and dried ti leaves and a strand of yellow ilima are threaded between them. Late afternoon sun slants across, so each nut carries a bright window reflection and a soft warm shadow on the weave. Render the mat in burnt umber and straw-yellow watercolour hatched with fine pencil to show every plaited strip. The nuts are built in layered sepia and Payne's grey glazes with crisp lifted highlights. The rhythm is a calm, repeating curve.

A hyperreal close crop of a rickshaw's rear panel: a chrome bicycle bell, plastic tassels, mirrored star appliqués and a hand-painted peacock just behind them. Colours are loud and glossy, with enamel magenta, parrot green, chrome yellow and electric cyan in opaque marker fills, each shape bounded by crisp black pen lines. The bell's chrome surface reflects the whole street in distorted curves. Hard specular highlights are left as bare paper. Midday glare flattens the shadows, so everything reads as saturated and gleaming, and decoration crowds every centimetre of the frame.
